title: Compact regular-module image propagates an adjunction unit
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded $\mathbf Z$-algebra is an associative unital graded ring with a degree-one additive differential $d$, $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$ for homogeneous $a,b$. A right dg module has $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m\,d(a)$ and $d^2=0$. Its derived category $D(A,d)$ is the homotopy category of right dg modules localized at cohomology isomorphisms, with the mapping-cone triangles and integer shifts. Let $(A,d)$ be such a dg algebra. Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with all small coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Give exact functors $T:D(A,d)\to\mathcal T$ and $R:\mathcal T\to D(A,d)$ and a specified shift-compatible adjunction $T\dashv R$ with unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to RT$. Suppose that $T$ preserves all small coproducts, that $T(A)$ is compact in $\mathcal T$ [def-pc-compact-object], and that $\eta_A:A\to RT(A)$ is an isomorphism. Then $\eta_M:M\to RT(M)$ is an isomorphism for every $M\in D(A,d)$, and $T$ is fully faithful, meaning it induces a bijection on every morphism set. No generation assumption on $T(A)$ in $\mathcal T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09LZ (lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case), proof by property-(P) resolutions and coproducts, stated in its relative form: only compactness in the actual target category of the tensor functor is used, not compactness in a larger ambient category.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal D=D(A,d)$. Coproducts are dg-module direct sums by [lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle]. By [lem-sfb-dg-free-shift-derived-hom], $f\mapsto[f(1)]$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(A[n],M)\cong H^{-n}(M)$, natural in dg-module maps $M\to M'$. Applied to the coprojections $M_i\to\bigoplus_iM_i$, it turns the canonical map $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(A[n],M_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(A[n],\bigoplus_iM_i)$ into $\bigoplus_iH^{-n}(M_i)\to H^{-n}(\bigoplus_iM_i)$. Cycles and boundaries in a direct sum are componentwise with finite support, so this map is bijective and every $A[n]$ is compact by [def-pc-compact-object]. Also $T(A[n])\simeq T(A)[n]$ is compact: apply the inverse shift to the target coproduct and use compactness of $T(A)$; shifts, being equivalences, preserve coproducts.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S=\{A[n]\mid n\in\mathbf Z\}$. Its localizing closure, meaning the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory closed under all small coproducts and containing $\mathcal S$, is all of $\mathcal D$: its object property satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-devissage]. Therefore [lem-sf-localizing-hom-test] applies to every morphism of $\mathcal D$ and makes $\mathcal S$ an isomorphism-testing family. All indices and Hom sets are taken in the fixed common universe of the statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-compact-tests-right-adjoint-coproducts] with $C=\mathcal D$, $D=\mathcal T$, left adjoint $T$, right adjoint $R$, and the small family $G_n=A[n]$. Step 1 gives compactness of $G_n$ and $T(G_n)$, and step 2 gives the required detection of isomorphisms in the source. Both categories have the specified coproducts and Hom sets in the chosen universe. Hence $R$ preserves all small coproducts. Explicitly the comparison $\bigoplus_i RY_i\to R(\bigoplus_iY_i)$ is tested by $\operatorname{Hom}(A[n],-)$; adjunction and compactness identify both sides with $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(T(A[n]),Y_i)$, with the comparison becoming the identity by naturality on each coprojection.

proof.text: Consider $Q(M):\Leftrightarrow\eta_{M[n]}$ is an isomorphism for every integer $n$. The identity and $RT$ are exact and preserve small coproducts (for $RT$, use the hypothesis on $T$ and step 3). Thus [lem-sc-shift-saturated-iso-locus] makes $Q$ invariant under isomorphisms and closed under shifts, coproducts and distinguished triangles. Shift compatibility of the specified adjunction identifies $\eta_{A[k]}$ with the shift of $\eta_A$ conjugated by the structural shift isomorphism, so $Q(A[k])$ holds for every $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-devissage] to $Q$. It holds on every object, and its $n=0$ clause says that every $\eta_M$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 09LZ, lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case, property-(P) and compactness argument, in the stated abstract adjunction form; Tag 0FQE, remark-P-resolution.

proof.text: For $M,N\in\mathcal D$, adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(TM,TN)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(M,RTN)$. Postcompose with $\eta_N^{-1}$ to obtain a bijection to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(M,N)$. Naturality of the adjunction says that $T(f)$ maps first to $\eta_N\circ f$, and hence to $f$. Thus this bijection is inverse to the map induced by $T$ on every Hom set, proving full faithfulness. The only target compactness used was that of the shifts of $T(A)$; no target-generation hypothesis entered.
